newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ukraine calls for Japan cash for space industry.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine calls for Japan cash for space industry.

text.p: Ukraine Foreign Minister Gennady Udovenko called on Tuesday for Japanese cooperation in space exploration following U.S. criticism over Ukraine's rocket programme.

"I met with top Japanese business leaders and discussed increasing Japanese investment in the Ukraine... including joint projects in space exploration, aerospace and the shipbuilding sector," he told reporters.

Udovenkov's remarks came after Ukraine's top security official on Monday rejected U.S. pressure to scrap Kiev's rocket programme, which includes 300- and 500-kilometre range missiles and rockets capable of launching satellites.
Washington fears the missiles could be sold to states like Libya, Iraq and Iran but Kiev has denied it would sell rockets to "countries whose moral standing is in question".
Ukraine's Yuzhmash plant, in the eastern industrial city of Dnipropetrovsk, is the world's largest rocket production facility.

Udovenko said the first post-Soviet deal with Russia, aimed at settling disagreements over the use of the Black Sea fleet and Sebastopol naval base, had been fixed but refused to divulge details of the accord.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin is due to sign the treaty during his May 30 and 31 visit to the Ukraine.
Udovenko added that a major aim of his trip to Japan was to draw Japanese investment to bolster reform of Ukraine's newly capitalist economy and the country's administrative system.
